newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms reject bids for 25,000T U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms reject bids for 25,000T U.S. wheat.

text.p: Two Philippine flour millers rejected on Friday bids for the supply of 25,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said.
"The firms said prices submitted were too high," one trader who joined the tender told Reuters.

Grains traders submitted a price of over $200 per tonne FOB for dark northern spring wheat and at least $183 per tonne for western white wheat, an executive in one of the Philippine mills told Reuters.
Last week, price of dark northern spring wheat was pegged at $198 per tonne FOB while western white wheat fetched $180 per tonne.
"Rumours that Pakistan may buy around 350,000 tonnes of wheat at the weekend inflated prices of U.S. wheat." the Philippine flour executive said.
"We will look at the market again next week. We will buy on price dips," he added.
